examples.en: Every autumn we go see the fall leaves.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 매해 새 제품을 내놓아요.
examples.en: That company releases a new product every year.
Every year on my birthday I have a meal with my family.
It rains a lot around this time every year.
The festival is held every year, so I look forward to it.
I save a little bit every year.

explain: '매년'과 같은 뜻이지만 '매해'는 조금 더 부드럽고 글이나 이야기 느낌이 있어요. 말할 때는 '해마다'나 '매년'이 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Every year I go on a trip with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매해'와 뜻은 같지만 말할 때 더 자주 쓰는 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 매해 but more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: I have seaweed soup every year on my birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '매해'보다 자연스럽고 친근한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more natural and friendly in speech than 매해.

explain_en: Same meaning as 매년, but 매해 sounds softer and a bit more written or storylike. In speech, 해마다 and 매년 come up more often.

dis.h: Sino prefix plus native 'year'; less common
gh: Sino-Korean form; neutral, common in writing

p.n: Same meaning; 매해 is used less often than the other two.

t90.ax: I save a little bit every year.

examples.en: The draw is done at random.
The songs play in random order.
We split the students into two groups at random.
Drawing numbers randomly is fair.

examples.ko: 무작위 선택이라서 누구도 결과를 알 수 없어요.
examples.en: It is a random pick, so no one can know the result.
Emails were sent out at random, which caused a problem.

explain: 주로 '무작위로'나 '무작위 + 명사'(무작위 추첨)로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '랜덤'을 더 자주 쓰고, '무작위'는 설명이나 뉴스 말투예요. '아무렇게나'는 대충 한다는 느낌이 있어서 달라요.

phrases.en: I picked a card at random.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무작위로'에 동사를 붙인 쓰임으로, 규칙 없이 뽑거나 고를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '무작위로' plus a verb, used when picking or choosing without any rule.

phrases.en: Please play the songs on random.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. '무작위'는 설명이나 뉴스 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but more casual in everyday talk. 무작위 sounds like explanations or news.

phrases.en: The computer makes a random selection.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무작위' 뒤에 명사를 붙인 글 말투로, 설명문이나 설정 화면에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A written-style noun phrase, often seen in explanations and settings screens.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '무작위로' or '무작위 + noun' (무작위 추첨, a random draw). In casual speech 랜덤 is more common; 무작위 sounds like explanations and news. 아무렇게나 means doing it carelessly, so it is different.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 수적으로 불리했지만 끝까지 싸웠어요.
examples.en: Our team was at a numerical disadvantage but fought to the end.

examples.ko: 수적 우위를 믿고 방심하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't let your guard down just because you outnumber them.
In terms of numbers, we have far more people.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 수적 열세를 극복하고 이겼어요.
examples.en: Our team overcame being outnumbered and won.
The difference in numbers is not big.
Qualitative change is more important than change in numbers.

explain: '수적 우위', '수적 열세'처럼 명사 앞에 쓰고, '수적으로'의 꼴로 많이 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '질적'이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '숫자상으로', '숫자로는'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Our team won despite being outnumbered.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수적 우위'의 반대로, 사람 수가 상대보다 적은 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 수적 우위; being fewer in number than the other side.

phrases.example: 수적 우위를 이용해서 경기를 쉽게 풀었어요.
phrases.en: They used their numerical advantage to play the game easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 수가 상대보다 많은 유리한 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A favorable situation of having more people than the other side.

phrases.en: Female students outnumber the others.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수적으로'는 숫자로 따졌을 때라는 뜻으로 서술어를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: '수적으로' means 'in terms of numbers' and modifies the predicate.

explain_en: It goes before a noun, as in '수적 우위' (numerical superiority) and '수적 열세' (numerical disadvantage), and is often used in the form '수적으로'. Its counterpart is '질적' (qualitative). In daily talk people also say '숫자상으로' or '숫자로는'.

examples.en: This painting sold for tens of millions of won.
Tens of millions of people listened to this song.
Dinosaurs lived tens of millions of years ago.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 수천만 달러를 벌었다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that movie earned tens of millions of dollars.

examples.ko: 집을 사려면 수천만 원이 더 필요해요.
examples.en: To buy a house, I need tens of millions of won more.

examples.ko: 수천만 개의 별이 하늘에 떠 있어요.
examples.en: Tens of millions of stars are floating in the sky.

explain: 한국어는 만 단위로 세기 때문에 '수천만'은 천만 단위가 몇 번 들어간 큰 수예요. '수천 만'처럼 띄지 않고 붙여 쓰고, 보통 '수천만 원', '수천만 명'처럼 단위 앞에 와요. '몇천만'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: That bag costs tens of millions of won.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수천만'과 뜻이 같고, 대화에서 '몇천만 원'처럼 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 수천만; often used in conversation, as in '몇천만 원'.

phrases.en: I looked at a watch worth tens of millions of won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값이 매우 비싼 물건을 말할 때 '짜리'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 짜리 to describe the price of an expensive item.
phrases.en_equiv: worth tens of millions of won

phrases.en: This app has been downloaded tens of millions of times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 많은 물건의 수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a very large number of things.

explain_en: Korean counts in units of 만 (10,000), so 수천만 is a big number made of several thousands of 만, i.e. tens of millions. Write it together, not as '수천 만', and it usually comes before a unit, as in '수천만 원' or '수천만 명'. You can also say '몇천만'.

examples.en: The Korean athletes swept the gold medals.
Customers cleaned out everything at the mart.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 음원 차트를 싹쓸이하고 있어요.
examples.en: That singer is sweeping the music charts.
If fishing boats take every fish, the sea is ruined.

examples.ko: 우리 반이 상을 싹쓸이할 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I didn't expect our class to sweep all the prizes.

examples.ko: 사람들이 마스크를 싹쓸이해서 살 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: People bought up all the masks, so I couldn't get any.

explain: '상을, 메달을, 차트를, 물건을'처럼 목적어에 '를'을 붙여 써요. 상을 휩쓰는 좋은 뜻도 되고, 물건을 사재기하는 부정적인 뜻도 돼요. '휩쓸다'는 태풍처럼 널리 영향을 줄 때도 쓰지만, '싹쓸이하다'는 남김없이 다 가져간다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Our country swept all the medals in archery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 종목의 메달을 모두 가져갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one side takes all the medals in an event.

phrases.en: People bought up all the ramen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 남김없이 사 가는 부정적인 느낌도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can have a negative feel of buying everything up.

phrases.example: 다른 사람도 써야 하니까 싹쓸이하지 마세요.
phrases.en: Others need some too, so please don't take everything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모두 가져가지 말라고 공손히 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request not to take everything.

explain_en: Take every last item or prize — informal, often a bit negative. It takes an object marked with '를', as in '상을, 메달을, 차트를, 물건을'. It can be positive, as in winning all the prizes, or negative, as in hoarding goods. '휩쓸다' can also mean a storm sweeping across a wide area, but '싹쓸이하다' stresses taking everything with nothing left.

t90.ax: That singer is sweeping the music charts.

examples.en: I cooked the rice with green peas in it.
The child picked out only the peas to eat.

examples.ko: 마트에서 냉동 완두콩을 한 봉지 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a bag of frozen peas at the mart.
When you peel the pod, peas come out in a row.
Fried rice looks nicer with peas in it.
Pea soup is smooth and sweet.

explain: '콩'의 한 종류라서 이름 끝에 '콩'이 붙어요. 초록색 알은 밥이나 볶음밥, 떡에 넣어 먹어요. '강낭콩', '검은콩' 같은 다른 콩도 많아서 색과 모양으로 구분해요.

phrases.en: Pea rice is sweet and tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥에 완두콩을 넣어 지은 음식 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of rice cooked with peas.

phrases.en: Grandma is shelling peas.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완두콩'의 짧은 말로, 까거나 삶는 일 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of 완두콩, common when talking about shelling or cooking.

phrases.en: I boiled peas and put them in the salad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when cooking.

explain_en: It ends in 콩 because it is a kind of bean. The green seeds go into rice, fried rice and rice cakes. There are many other beans such as 강낭콩 and 검은콩, which are told apart by color and shape.

examples.ko: 이 월간지는 매달 첫째 주에 나와요.
examples.en: This monthly magazine comes out in the first week of each month.
I have a regular subscription to a monthly magazine.
My photo was published in a monthly magazine.
I bought the fashion monthly to get the bonus gift.
I borrowed a back issue of the monthly magazine from the library.

examples.ko: 월간지 기사를 쓰는 일을 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work writing articles for a monthly magazine.

explain: 한 달에 한 번 나오는 잡지예요. 일주일에 한 번 나오면 '주간지', 석 달에 한 번이면 '계간지'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I bought a monthly magazine at the bookstore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 권씩 살 때 쓰는 가장 쉬운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easiest collocation for buying a single issue.

phrases.en: My writing was published in a monthly magazine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 사진이 잡지에 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when writing or photos appear in a magazine.
phrases.en_equiv: to be published in a monthly magazine

phrases.en: This month's magazine is out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 호가 나왔을 때 시기를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the time tells which issue has come out.

explain_en: It is a magazine published once a month. One published weekly is a '주간지', and one published quarterly is a '계간지'.

examples.en: There were a lot of visitors at the amusement park today.

examples.ko: 입장객은 모두 손목에 도장을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: All entrants have to get a stamp on their wrist.
The number of museum visitors rose compared with last year.
They give free water bottles to people who enter.
Because of the rain, the number of visitors was cut in half.
The visitors are lining up and waiting.

explain: 공연장, 박물관, 경기장처럼 어딘가에 들어온 사람을 셀 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '입장객 수'로 자주 나와요. '관람객'은 보러 온 사람이라는 점이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: A thousand visitors come to the museum each day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어온 사람보다 보러 온 사람이라는 뜻이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes people who came to see something rather than just entering.

phrases.en: The number of visitors this year increased from last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 안내문에서 사람 수를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news or notices when giving visitor counts.

phrases.en: Today we are admitting only five hundred visitors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운영하는 쪽에서 사람을 들여보낼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the organizer letting people in.

explain_en: It is used when counting people who entered a venue such as a concert hall, museum or stadium. In the news it often appears as '입장객 수'. '관람객' puts more focus on people who came to watch something.

t90.ax: The visitors are lining up and waiting.

examples.ko: 장년층을 겨냥한 건강 검진 상품이 최근 많이 나오고 있어요.
examples.en: Many health checkup packages aimed at the middle-aged group have come out recently.

examples.ko: 장년층 취업 지원 프로그램이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new job support program for middle-aged people has started.

examples.ko: 장년층은 운동 부족으로 건강이 나빠지기 쉬워요.
examples.en: Middle-aged people can easily lose health from lack of exercise.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 청년층보다 장년층이 더 많이 써요.
examples.en: More middle-aged people use this app than young people.
A large-print menu is convenient for middle-aged people.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 장년층 인구가 점점 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The middle-aged population in our neighborhood is gradually growing.

explain: 청년층과 노년층 사이의 나이대 사람들을 가리켜요. 정확한 나이 범위는 글이나 통계마다 달라서, '중장년층'이라고 묶어 말하기도 해요. 뉴스, 광고, 통계에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: This program is popular with middle-aged and older adults.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중년층과 장년층을 함께 묶어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Groups the middle-aged and the somewhat older together.

phrases.en: The number of middle-aged customers has grown a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 광고에서 나이대로 손님을 나눌 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in shops and ads when dividing customers by age.

phrases.en: It's an event where young and middle-aged people join together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이대를 비교하거나 함께 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used to compare or mention age groups together.

explain_en: It refers to people in the age range between young adults and seniors. The exact age range varies by article or statistic, and people often group it as '중장년층'. It frequently appears in news, ads and statistics.

examples.en: The government announced a plan to increase rice production.

examples.ko: 겨울이 오기 전에 석유 증산이 필요하다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news saying oil production needs to rise before winter.

examples.ko: 공장은 증산을 위해 직원을 더 뽑고 있어요.
examples.en: The factory is hiring more workers to boost production.

examples.ko: 증산 결정 이후 가격이 조금 내려갔어요.
examples.en: Prices dropped a little after the decision to raise production.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 올해 반도체 증산에 힘을 쏟고 있어요.
examples.en: This company is putting great effort into producing more chips this year.

examples.ko: 농민들은 증산보다 품질이 더 중요하다고 말해요.
examples.en: Farmers say quality matters more than higher output.

explain: 반대말은 '감산'이에요. 쌀, 석유, 반도체처럼 만들어 내는 물건의 양을 늘린다는 뉴스에서 주로 나와요. 일상에서는 '더 많이 만들다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The company made a production increase plan this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생산을 늘리려는 계획을 말할 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for plans to raise production.

phrases.en: This year's production increase target is 10 percent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자와 함께 늘릴 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with numbers to state how much to increase.

phrases.en: Prices fell, so they decided to cut production.
phrases.nuance_ko: '증산'의 반대말로, 생산량을 줄이는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '증산', meaning reducing output.

explain_en: Its opposite is '감산' (production cut). It mostly appears in news about raising the output of goods such as rice, oil or chips. In daily talk people say '더 많이 만들다'.

examples.en: This disease doesn't have a high fatality rate.
The fatality rate of the flu differs by age.

examples.ko: 치사율이 낮아도 감염 속도가 빠르면 위험해요.
examples.en: Even if the fatality rate is low, it's dangerous if the infection spreads fast.
The news announced the fatality rate of the new virus.
The fatality rate and the infection rate are different numbers.
I heard the fatality rate dropped a lot after vaccination.

explain: 병에 걸린 사람 중에서 목숨을 잃는 사람의 비율이에요. 전체 인구를 기준으로 하는 '사망률'과는 기준이 달라요. 감염병 뉴스에서 '치사율이 높다/낮다'로 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 감기는 치사율이 낮아서 크게 걱정하지 않아도 돼요.
phrases.en: This cold has a low fatality rate, so you don't need to worry much.
phrases.nuance_ko: '높다'의 반대로 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The common opposite of '치사율이 높다'.

phrases.example: 치사율이 높은 병은 빨리 치료해야 해요.
phrases.en: A disease with a high fatality rate must be treated quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 활용형 '높은'으로 병을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier '높은' describes the disease.

phrases.en: Quick treatment lowers the fatality rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료나 대책의 효과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the effect of treatment or measures.

explain_en: It is the share of people with a disease who die from it. This differs from '사망률' (death rate), which is based on the whole population. In infectious disease news you often hear '치사율이 높다/낮다'.

en: big spender; high roller; major investor

examples.ko: 그는 부동산 시장의 큰손으로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: He is known as a big player in the real estate market.

examples.ko: 해외 큰손들이 국내 주식을 사고 있어요.
examples.en: Big overseas investors are buying domestic stocks.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 큰손 손님이 오면 특별히 챙겨 줘요.
examples.en: This shop takes special care of big-spending customers.

examples.ko: 경매장에 큰손이 나타나서 가격이 확 올랐어요.
examples.en: A big buyer showed up at the auction and the price shot up.
Stock prices swing a lot depending on what the big players do.

examples.ko: 저는 큰손은 아니지만 매달 조금씩 투자해요.
examples.en: I'm not a big player, but I invest a little every month.

explain: 손이 큰 사람이 아니라, 증권·부동산·경매처럼 돈이 오가는 곳에서 큰돈을 움직이는 사람을 말해요. 반대로 적은 돈으로 투자하는 개인 투자자는 '개미'라고 해요. 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, 가게에서는 돈을 많이 쓰는 손님을 가리키기도 해요.

phrases.en: The big players in the stock market are buying up shares.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주식 시장에서 큰돈을 움직이는 사람을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for people who move large sums in the stock market.

phrases.example: 백화점은 큰손 고객을 위해 특별한 서비스를 준비했어요.
phrases.en: The department store prepared special services for its big-spending customers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 돈을 아주 많이 쓰는 손님을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to customers who spend a great deal at a store.

phrases.example: 큰손 투자자가 이 회사에 투자했다는 소식이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is news that a major investor has invested in this company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투자하는 금액이 아주 큰 사람을 말해요. 작은 개인 투자자인 '개미'와 반대예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who invests very large sums; the opposite of the small retail investor '개미'.

explain_en: It does not mean someone with large hands; it means a person who moves a lot of money in places like the stock market, real estate or auctions. Small individual investors are called '개미' (ants). It often appears in the news, and shops also use it for customers who spend a lot.

en: common year; normal year; average year

examples.en: This winter was much warmer than usual.

examples.ko: 평년에는 이맘때 비가 많이 안 와요.
examples.en: In a normal year, it does not rain much around this time.
This summer's temperature is at the usual level.
Unlike a normal year, last year's autumn was short.

examples.ko: 올해 사과 수확량이 평년의 두 배예요.
examples.en: This year's apple harvest is twice that of a normal year.

examples.ko: 평년 때보다 눈이 훨씬 적게 내렸어요.
examples.en: Much less snow fell than in a normal year.

explain: 날씨 뉴스에서는 지난 30년쯤의 평균을 '평년'이라고 해요. '평년보다 높다', '평년보다 낮다'로 자주 써요. 달력에서는 윤년이 아닌 해, 곧 2월이 28일인 해도 평년이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: Today's temperature is higher than normal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨 뉴스에서 평균과 비교할 때 가장 흔히 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pattern in weather news when comparing with the average.

phrases.example: 이번 주 기온은 평년 기온과 비슷해요.
phrases.en: This week's temperature is similar to the normal temperature.
phrases.nuance_ko: '평년'을 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 평균 날씨를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '평년' goes before another noun to refer to average weather.

phrases.en: This year's rainfall is similar to normal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평균과 거의 같을 때 쓰고, '평년보다'는 차이가 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it's about the same as average; '평년보다' is used when there is a difference.

explain_en: Ordinary non-leap year with 28-day February; also a climate norm year. In weather news, 평년 refers to the average over roughly the last 30 years, as in 평년보다 높다 or 평년보다 낮다. In the calendar, a year that is not a leap year, when February has 28 days, is also called a 평년.

examples.ko: 올해 후반기에는 여행을 많이 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I plan to travel a lot in the second half of this year.
Now that it is the second half, work has gotten much busier.

examples.ko: 야구 시즌 후반기에 우리 팀이 강해졌어요.
examples.en: Our team got stronger in the second half of the baseball season.
Classes for the second half start in September.

examples.ko: 회사는 후반기 계획을 다시 짜고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is redoing its plans for the second half.
The further into the second half of the season, the more intense the games get.

explain: 한 해나 시즌, 학기를 반으로 나눈 뒤쪽이에요. 앞쪽은 '전반기'예요. 경기 하나의 뒷부분은 '후반전'이라고 하고, 한 해에서는 '하반기'도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I will start a new job in the second half of the year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 해의 뒤쪽 반을 말할 때 '후반기'보다 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common than '후반기' for the second half of a year.

phrases.en: Let's make our plans for the second half together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '계획'과 함께 써서 뒤쪽 시기의 일정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with 'plan' to talk about the later period's schedule.

phrases.en: The second half is hard because there are many exams.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에는'을 붙여 뒤쪽 시기를 앞 시기와 비교해 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '에는' contrasts the later period with the earlier one.

explain_en: Second half of a year or term, business and schedule usage. It is the latter half of a year, season, or semester. The first half is '전반기'. The second part of a single game is '후반전', and for a year '하반기' is also common.

t90.ax: Classes for the second half start in September.
